summary: Tested the new 'Welkomstmail' feature end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_welcome.py pass - (1) POST /api/customers {send_welcome:true, email:delivered@resend.dev} creates user (role=customer, customer_id linked) + password_reset_tokens doc (purpose='welcome', used=false, expires ~7 days), returns welcome_sent_at; (2) send_welcome without email just no-ops (no welcome_sent_at, no user); (3) duplicate email (bas@white-vision.nl) returns 400 with 'account' message and rolls back the inserted customer (no orphan); (4) rate limit returns 429 after 3 welcome tokens exist in last hour (seeded synthetically to avoid upstream email rate limits); (5) DJ (bas@) POST /api/customers/{id}/welcome -> 403; (6) raw welcome token inserted via mongo + POST /api/auth/reset-password works, user can then log in; (7) regression: send_welcome=false + password still creates login that can log in. Frontend (Playwright): checkbox 'person-send-welcome-checkbox' is checked by default and hides 'person-password-input'; unchecking shows it; re-checking hides it. Client-side toast 'Vul een e-mailadres in voor de welkomstmail' appears when saving without email. Creating customer with delivered+ui<ts>@resend.dev + welcome -> card shows 'Heeft login' badge, welcome-status 'Welkomstmail zojuist', button becomes 'Opnieuw sturen'. Opened /wachtwoord-herstellen?token=<raw>&welkom=1: eyebrow 'Welkom bij White Vision', H1 'Stel je wachtwoord in'. Setting password reaches reset-success, then login with new password lands on customer page with 'Welkom, TEST_UIWelkom / Je event wordt op dit moment klaargezet' empty-state. All test data cleaned up (customers, users, tokens, login_attempts).
critical_code_review_comments: mailer.send_email is awaited inline inside the request handler. The Emergent email proxy aggressively rate-limits (observed HTTP 429 after ~4 rapid sends in one test run), so a single admin burst (one create + three resends) can hit the upstream limit. Our backend converts that into a 502 'Welkomstmail kon niet worden verstuurd' and welcome_error on the create response. Consider: (a) using BackgroundTasks for the actual send so the API returns fast; (b) retry-with-backoff on upstream 429; (c) distinguishing 'provider rate limit' from 'send failure' in the UI toast.

routes/admin.py:_send_welcome inserts a password_reset_tokens row BEFORE the send_email call. On upstream failure the row is left behind and still counts toward the 3/hour rate limit. If upstream fails 3 times in a row the next genuine attempt will be blocked by our own 429 even though no email ever arrived. Suggest issuing the token only after a successful send, or deleting the token on send failure.

routes/admin.py:create_customer: if send_welcome=true and _send_welcome raises a non-400 HTTPException (e.g. 502), the customer and user are kept and welcome_error is returned. That is probably desired (admin can retry via /welcome), but the frontend AdminPeople.jsx submit shows toast.error('Klant aangemaakt, maar: ...') and then does NOT also call toast.success('Klant opgeslagen') — reasonable. Confirm this is intentional.
No TTL index on db.password_reset_tokens.expires_at — expired/used tokens accumulate (same as iteration 4 note).

POST /api/customers with send_welcome=true but no email just silently drops the welcome (no error, no welcome_sent_at). The frontend blocks this client-side, but the backend contract would be clearer with a 400 'E-mailadres vereist voor welkomstmail' for defense in depth.

Welcome email HTML uses a 7-day link but reuses the generic password_reset_tokens collection; purpose field is the only discriminator. Fine, but consider logging/auditing which tokens are 'welcome' vs 'reset' separately.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Welcome email flow is fully working. test_welcome.py is safe to re-run — the only test that actually calls the Emergent email proxy is test_create_customer_with_welcome; it skips (not fails) when the provider rate-limits. All other tests use mongo-direct token insertion so they do not depend on real email delivery. Do NOT run it more than ~once per minute in rapid succession because the upstream email provider has a short rate-limit window.
